ADVISORY FOR TAXPAYERS AND TAX PROFESSIONALS
June 9, 2026

June Estimated Payment Due Date Reminder
PROVIDENCE, R.I. – The Rhode Island Division of Taxation reminds taxpayers and tax
professionals of the June 15 due date for the second installment of many estimated
payments, which apply to some personal income filers and many business entities.
The tax types for which the upcoming June 15 due date applies are outlined below:

June 15 Due Date for These Filings and Related Payments

Personal income tax – estimate
Corporate income tax – estimate

The table above provides only a summary of certain estimated payment filings; for details on due dates for these and other tax types/forms/entities, see the
Division of Taxation’s website: www.tax.ri.gov.

The Division also reminds taxpayers and tax professionals that the Rhode Island Tax
Portal (https://taxportal.ri.gov/) is the best way to file and pay most business taxes. If
you are subject to Rhode Island’s Electronic Filing Mandate, filing and paying on the
Portal will help you meet the requirements of the Mandate.
Remember, if you are subject to the Electronic Filing Mandate the best way to do so is
by creating a Portal account. To do so, you must create a Portal User ID, and you must
link your User ID to your tax accounts. This is done by entering a PIN number that
arrives in a PIN notice sent by the Division via postal mail. If you are close to the due
date and do not have a Portal account set up, you can pay using the Same-day Services
Guest Payment feature.
For questions about Personal Income tax, contact the Rhode Island Division of
Taxation’s Personal Income Tax Taxpayer Assistance Section at: Tax.Assist@tax.ri.gov,
or by telephone at: (401) 574-8829, option #3, between 8:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. on
business days.
For questions about corporate taxes, contact the Rhode Island Division of Taxation’s
Corporate Income Tax Section at Tax.Corporate@tax.ri.gov, or by phone at (401) 5748829, option #6 between 8:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. on business days.
The Rhode Island Division of Taxation, part of the Rhode Island Department of Revenue, is open to the
public from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. business days. For more information, contact the Division of Taxation
at (401) 574‐8829 or see https://tax.ri.gov/about-us/contact-us.
